directAnswer: To use a Git branch, you can create a new branch, switch to it, and then commit changes independently from the main branch.
summary: This guide explains how to create, switch, and manage branches in Git, allowing for parallel development.

sections.heading: Creating a Branch
sections.body: Use the command `git branch <branch-name>` to create a new branch. This does not switch to the new branch immediately.

sections.heading: Switching Branches
sections.body: To switch to a branch, use `git checkout <branch-name>`. In newer versions of Git, you can also use `git switch <branch-name>`.

sections.heading: Merging Branches
sections.body: To merge changes from one branch into another, switch to the target branch and use `git merge <branch-name>`.

steps.title: Create a new branch
steps.detail: Run `git branch feature-xyz` to create a new branch named 'feature-xyz'.

steps.title: Switch to the new branch
steps.detail: Execute `git checkout feature-xyz` or `git switch feature-xyz` to start working on the new branch.

steps.title: Make changes and commit
steps.detail: After making changes, stage them with `git add .` and commit using `git commit -m 'Your message'`.

steps.title: Merge changes back to main branch
steps.detail: Switch back to the main branch with `git checkout main` and merge your changes using `git merge feature-xyz`.

faqs.question: What is the difference between `git checkout` and `git switch`?
faqs.answer: `git checkout` can be used for both switching branches and restoring files, while `git switch` is specifically for switching branches.

faqs.question: Can I delete a branch after merging?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can delete a branch using `git branch -d <branch-name>` after merging it, but ensure that you no longer need it.

faqs.question: How do I see all branches in my repository?
faqs.answer: Use the command `git branch` to list all local branches, and `git branch -a` to see both local and remote branches.

caveats: Merging branches can lead to conflicts if changes overlap; resolve conflicts before completing the merge.
Ensure you commit or stash changes before switching branches to avoid losing work.
